mainTopic: Why painting a fruit-dropping tree red is allowed despite looking like a superstitious 'Amorite practice': it lets people see the tree's trouble and pray for it. Closing of the פרק בהמה המקשה.
overview: The amud opens by finishing a discussion about a tree that drops its fruit too early. Weighing it down with stones is allowed because it weakens the tree. Painting it red is allowed because it gets people to notice and pray for it, so it is not דרכי האמורי. A ברייתא learns from the מצורע's call of 'טמא טמא' that anyone in trouble should tell the public so they will pray, and רבינא explains a custom of hanging dates on a palm the same way. Then the פרק בהמה המקשה ends, and a new פרק begins. Its משנה teaches that the איסור of אותו ואת בנו, slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day, applies everywhere, at all times, to both חולין and קדשים. The משנה then goes through many combinations of ordinary and holy animals, slaughtered inside or outside the עזרה. For each one it says who gets כרת, who gets lashes, and which animal is fit. The גמרא brings a ברייתא that learns from two neighboring פסוקים that the rule covers קדשים. It uses the words 'שור' and 'ושור' to show that the rule covers both kinds of animals. Finally, the גמרא asks why the rule includes mixed breeds (כלאים), and begins a second challenge from a teaching of רבא that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Stones make sense, but why the red paint?
steps.stepSummary: Loading the tree with stones is understandable because it weakens the tree. But what is the point of painting it red?
steps.simpleTranslation: [The stones are fine] so that its strength will weaken. But painting it with red paint — why?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finishes explaining why stones are allowed (they weaken the tree), then asks what useful purpose the red paint could have.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A practice is only allowed, and not treated as superstition, if it has a real, sensible purpose. The stones have one: they cut down the tree's overload of blossoms. Red paint does nothing to the tree physically, so the גמרא asks why it is permitted.

keyTerms.meaning: But; here it moves from the easy case to the hard one

steps.confusionAlert: This step begins in the middle of a sentence. The first words finish the earlier line: 'It makes sense to load it with stones, so that its strength weakens.'

phrases.english: so that its strength will weaken,
but painting it with red paint, why?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the earlier discussion of permitted treatments for a fruit-dropping tree.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What real purpose does painting the tree red serve, so that it is not a forbidden superstitious practice?

steps.title: So people will see it and pray
steps.stepSummary: The red paint draws attention, so people who pass by will notice the tree's problem and pray for it.
steps.simpleTranslation: So that people will see it and ask for mercy on its behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the red paint is a signal to the public, so they will pray for the tree.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The purpose is not magic. It works the way a sign works, by getting people to pray. Since prayer is a real and proper goal, the practice is not superstition.

phrases.english: so that people will see it
and ask for mercy on its behalf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The red paint publicizes the tree's trouble so people will pray for it.

steps.title: The מצורע announces his trouble so people pray
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא learns from the פסוק 'טמא טמא יקרא' that a מצורע must tell the public, so they will pray for him. The same applies to anyone something bad happens to.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: 'And he shall call out: Impure, impure.' He must inform the public, and the public will ask for mercy on his behalf. Likewise, anyone to whom something happens must inform the public, and the public will ask for mercy on his behalf.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא to show that letting the public know about a trouble, so they will pray, is a real idea in the תורה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא reads the מצורע's call of 'טמא טמא' as more than a warning to stay away: it also asks for prayer. It then widens this to anyone in trouble. That gives a clear source for the tree case: making a problem known so others pray is a proper thing to do.

keyTerms.meaning: 'And he shall call out: Impure, impure.' The מצורע's announcement
Someone to whom something bad happened

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known source for asking others to pray for a sick or troubled person.

phrases.english: As it is taught:
'And he shall call out: Impure, impure' —
he must inform the public,
and the public will ask for mercy on his behalf.
And likewise, one to whom something happens —
must inform the public,
and the public will ask for mercy on his behalf.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a source that supports the answer in step 2.
steps.raayaObject: The idea that publicizing a trouble so others will pray is proper, not superstition.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא reading 'וטמא טמא יקרא' (ויקרא 13:45) as a call for public prayer, extended to anyone in trouble.

steps.title: רבינא: hanging date bunches on the palm follows this תנא
steps.stepSummary: רבינא says that the custom of hanging bunches of dates on a palm tree that drops its fruit is based on this תנא's idea of publicizing trouble.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבינא said: In accordance with whom do we hang bunches of dates on a palm tree? In accordance with whom? In accordance with this תנא.
steps.whatsHappening: רבינא uses the ברייתא to explain a custom of his own day: hanging date bunches on a struggling palm.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Hanging dates on a tree could look like a superstitious practice. רבינא says it is allowed for the same reason as the red paint: it shows passersby that the tree is in trouble, so they pray. He ties the custom to the תנא of the ברייתא just quoted.

keyTerms.meaning: In accordance with whom? Whose view does this follow?
A sage of the משנה or ברייתא period

steps.whatToRemember: Treatments for a fruit-dropping tree are allowed if they have a real purpose. Stones physically weaken the tree. Red paint and hanging dates publicize its trouble so people will pray, based on the מצורע who announces 'טמא טמא'.

phrases.english: Ravina said:
In accordance with whom do we hang bunches of dates on a palm tree,
in accordance with whom? In accordance with this תנא.
phrases.notes: 'This תנא' is the one from the ברייתא just quoted, who says to announce your trouble so people pray.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָבִינָא: כְּמַאן תָּלֵינַן כּוּבְסָא בְּדִיקְלָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the ברייתא to a practical custom.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Hanging date bunches on a fruit-dropping palm is allowed, following the ברייתא that troubles should be publicized so people will pray.

steps.title: Hadran — Closing בהמה המקשה
steps.stepSummary: The closing words that end the פרק בהמה המקשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: We will return to you, בהמה המקשה.
steps.whatsHappening: This line marks the end of the פרק called בהמה המקשה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The הדרן is a traditional closing that expresses the hope to come back and learn this פרק again. It is not part of the legal discussion.

keyTerms.meaning: We will return to you; the formula for finishing a פרק
'An animal having a difficult birth,' the name of this פרק

phrases.english: We will return to you, 'An animal having a difficult birth.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Closes the פרק after the final discussion.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The פרק בהמה המקשה is complete.

steps.title: The new פרק opens: the איסור of אותו ואת בנו applies everywhere
steps.stepSummary: The משנה states that the איסור of slaughtering a mother and its child on one day applies in every place, in every time period, and to both ordinary and holy animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: The rule of 'it and its child' applies both in the Land of Israel and outside the Land, both when the בית המקדש stands and when it does not, and to both ordinary animals and holy animals.
steps.whatsHappening: A brand-new פרק starts with a משנה that sets out how wide the איסור of אותו ואת בנו is.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids slaughtering an animal and its child on the same day. The משנה says this איסור is not tied to the Land, to the בית המקדש, or to the type of animal. It applies to חולין and to קדשים alike.

keyTerms.meaning: "It and its child": the איסור of slaughtering a mother animal and its offspring on the same day
When the בית המקדש is standing

steps.whyThisMatters: This tells us the מצוה is a personal איסור on the act of slaughtering. It is not a Temple law, so it still applies today.

phrases.english: MISHNA: The prohibition of 'it and its offspring'
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:28. These opening words are also the name of the new פרק.

phrases.aramaic: נוֹהֵג בֵּין בָּאָרֶץ בֵּין בְּחוּצָה לָאָרֶץ,
phrases.english: applies both in the Land and outside the Land,
in the presence of the Temple and not in the presence of the Temple,
to non-sacred animals and to sacrificial animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new פרק right after the הדרן that closed פרק בהמה המקשה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The איסור of אותו ואת בנו applies everywhere, at all times, to both חולין and קדשים.

steps.title: Case one: ordinary animals slaughtered outside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: If both animals are חולין and are slaughtered outside the עזרה, both may be eaten, but the person gets lashes for the second one.
steps.simpleTranslation: How does this work? If someone slaughters a mother and its child, both ordinary animals, outside the עזרה: both are fit to eat, and for the second one he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה asks 'How so?' and starts going through the cases one by one. This first case is the simplest one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering חולין outside is completely normal, so the first animal raises no problem. The second slaughter breaks the איסור of אותו ואת בנו, so the person gets מלקות. Still, the meat of the second animal is כשר. The איסור is on the act of slaughtering, not on the meat.

keyTerms.meaning: "How so?": introduces the details of a general rule

steps.confusionAlert: The second animal is still כשר to eat even though slaughtering it was an עבירה. The punishment is on the person, not on the meat.

phrases.english: How so?
One who slaughters it and its offspring,
non-sacred animals, outside the courtyard:
both of them are fit,
and for the second, he incurs the forty lashes.
phrases.notes: "Forty" is the standard name for מלקות, even though in practice the number given is thirty-nine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts spelling out the general rule of step 6 through specific cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין slaughtered outside: both are כשר, and there is מלקות for the second.

steps.title: Case two: holy animals slaughtered outside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: If both animals are קדשים and are slaughtered outside, the first brings כרת, both are פסול, and there are lashes for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy animals slaughtered outside: for the first one he is liable to כרת, both animals are disqualified, and he gets forty lashes for each of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves to holy animals that were slaughtered outside the עזרה, where a second איסור (שחוטי חוץ) gets involved.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה is punished with כרת, but only the first animal brings כרת. The second animal could not have been offered that day anyway, because of אותו ואת בנו. Both animals become פסול, and lashes are given for each slaughter: for the first, because it was a קרבן slaughtered outside, and for the second, because of אותו ואת בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals set aside as קרבנות
Disqualified (cannot be used as a קרבן)
The איסור of slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: Only the first animal brings כרת. The second does not, because on that day it was no longer fit to be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals, outside:
for the first, he is liable to karet,
and both of them are disqualified,
and for both of them he incurs the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Second case: holy animals instead of ordinary ones, still slaughtered outside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים slaughtered outside: כרת for the first, both are פסול, and there is מלקות for each.

steps.title: Case three: ordinary animals slaughtered inside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: If both animals are חולין and are slaughtered inside the עזרה, both are פסול, and there are lashes for the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: Ordinary animals slaughtered inside: both are disqualified, and for the second one he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now covers ordinary animals that were slaughtered inside the עזרה, a place meant only for קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Ordinary animals slaughtered in the עזרה become forbidden, so both are פסול. The first slaughter carries no lashes for אותו ואת בנו. The second slaughter breaks that איסור, so the person gets מלקות.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary animals slaughtered in the עזרה, which are forbidden

phrases.english: Non-sacred animals, inside:
both of them are unfit,
and for the second, he incurs the forty lashes;

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Third case: same ordinary animals as case one, but now slaughtered inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין slaughtered inside: both are פסול, and there is מלקות for the second.

steps.title: Case four: holy animals slaughtered inside the עזרה
steps.stepSummary: If both animals are קדשים and are slaughtered inside, the first is a proper קרבן with no punishment, while the second brings lashes and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: Holy animals slaughtered inside: the first is fit and he is exempt, but for the second he gets forty lashes and it is disqualified.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes this set of four cases with holy animals slaughtered in their proper place.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the first slaughter was done exactly right, so the first animal is כשר and there is no punishment. The second slaughter breaks אותו ואת בנו. That brings lashes and also makes the second animal פסול as a קרבן, because it was not allowed to be slaughtered that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Fit, here meaning valid as a קרבן

steps.whatToRemember: Four cases: (1) חולין outside: both are כשר, lashes for the second. (2) קדשים outside: כרת for the first, both are פסול, lashes for both. (3) חולין inside: both are פסול, lashes for the second. (4) קדשים inside: the first is כשר with no punishment, while the second is פסול with lashes.
steps.confusionAlert: Compare this with case one. There, the second ordinary animal stayed כשר to eat. Here, the second holy animal becomes פסול as a קרבן, because a קרבן must be fit to be offered at the time it is slaughtered.

phrases.english: Sacrificial animals, inside:
the first is fit and he is exempt,
and for the second, he incurs the forty lashes, and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Fourth case: holy animals as in case two, but now slaughtered inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים slaughtered inside: the first is כשר and there is no punishment, while the second is פסול and brings מלקות.

steps.title: First ordinary, second holy, both slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: If the first animal is חולין and the second is קדשים, and both are slaughtered outside the עזרה, the first is כשר with no punishment. The second brings lashes and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is ordinary and the second is holy, and both are slaughtered outside: the first is fine and there is no punishment. For the second he gets forty lashes, and it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה starts mixing the two types of animals. Here the ordinary animal is killed first and the holy one second, both outside the עזרה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first animal is a normal חולין שחיטה outside, so nothing is wrong with it. The second breaks אותו ואת בנו, so he gets lashes, and it is פסול as a קרבן. The משנה gives no כרת for the second animal, even though it is a קרבן slaughtered outside, because once its mother or child was slaughtered that day it could not have been offered anyway.

keyTerms.meaning: Holy animals set aside as קרבנות

steps.confusionAlert: Do not assume every קרבן slaughtered outside brings כרת. Here the second animal could not be offered that day because of אותו ואת בנו, so the משנה gives only lashes for it, with no כרת.

phrases.english: Ordinary and holy animals, outside —
phrases.notes: The first word is the animal slaughtered first. So the ordinary one is killed first, then the holy one.

phrases.english: the first is fit, and he is exempt,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes, and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the list of cases. After cases with two animals of the same type, the משנה now mixes the types.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין then קדשים outside: the first is כשר and פטור; the second brings lashes and is פסול.

steps.title: First holy, second ordinary, both slaughtered outside
steps.stepSummary: If the first animal is קדשים and the second is חולין, both outside, the first brings כרת and is פסול. The second is כשר, and he gets lashes for both.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is holy and the second is ordinary, both outside: for the first he is liable to כרת and it is unfit. The second is fit, and for both he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the order from the last case. Now the holy animal is killed first outside, and then the ordinary one.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first animal is a regular קרבן slaughtered outside (שחוטי חוץ), so it brings כרת and is פסול. The second is ordinary meat slaughtered properly, so it is כשר to eat, but it breaks אותו ואת בנו. That is why there are lashes for both: the first for slaughtering a קרבן outside, the second for אותו ואת בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: Spiritual cutting off, a heavenly punishment
Slaughtering a קרבן outside the עזרה

steps.confusionAlert: The second animal is כשר even though he gets lashes for it. Lashes for the act of slaughtering do not make the meat forbidden.

phrases.english: Holy and ordinary animals, outside —
for the first he is liable to כרת, and it is unfit,
and the second is fit,
and for both of them he receives the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the order of step 11, with the holy animal first and the ordinary one second.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים then חולין outside: the first brings כרת and is פסול; the second is כשר; there are lashes for both.

steps.title: First ordinary, second holy, both slaughtered inside
steps.stepSummary: If the first animal is חולין and the second is קדשים, both slaughtered inside the עזרה, both are פסול, and there are lashes for the second.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is ordinary and the second is holy, both inside: both are unfit, and for the second he gets forty lashes.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה moves the mixed cases inside the עזרה. The ordinary animal is killed first and the holy one second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: An ordinary animal slaughtered inside the עזרה is פסול, so the first animal is ruined. The second, a קרבן, is פסול because it is the child (or mother) of an animal already slaughtered today. He also gets lashes for the second because of אותו ואת בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: Ordinary animals slaughtered in the עזרה, which makes them forbidden

phrases.english: Ordinary and holy animals, inside —
both of them are unfit,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Applies the mixed order of step 11 to slaughtering inside the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חולין then קדשים inside: both are פסול; there are lashes for the second.

steps.title: First holy, second ordinary, both slaughtered inside
steps.stepSummary: If the first animal is קדשים and the second is חולין, both inside, the first is a valid קרבן with no punishment. The second brings lashes and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the first is holy and the second is ordinary, both inside: the first is fit and there is no punishment. For the second he gets forty lashes, and it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the order inside the עזרה. The holy animal is killed first and the ordinary one second.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first is a קרבן slaughtered in its proper place, so it is כשר and nothing is wrong. The second is ordinary meat slaughtered in the עזרה, so it is פסול, and it also breaks אותו ואת בנו, which brings lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: An offering brought in the בית המקדש

phrases.english: Holy and ordinary animals, inside —
the first is fit, and he is exempt,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes, and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reverses the order of step 13, still inside the עזרה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: קדשים then חולין inside: the first is כשר and פטור; the second brings lashes and is פסול.

steps.title: Two ordinary animals, the first outside and the second inside
steps.stepSummary: If both animals are חולין, with the first slaughtered outside and the second inside the עזרה, the first is כשר with no punishment. The second brings lashes and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both are ordinary, the first slaughtered outside and the second inside: the first is fit and there is no punishment. For the second he gets forty lashes, and it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה now changes the place within one pair. Both animals are ordinary, but one is killed outside and one inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first is a normal ordinary שחיטה outside, so it is fine. The second is ordinary meat slaughtered in the עזרה, which makes it פסול, and it breaks אותו ואת בנו, so he gets lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: The איסור of slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day

steps.whatToRemember: For each case, judge each animal on its own. Is it in the right place for its type (חולין outside, קדשים inside)? Then ask whether it is the second slaughter, which breaks אותו ואת בנו and brings lashes.

phrases.english: Ordinary animals, outside and inside —
the first is fit, and he is exempt,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes, and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After mixing the types of animal, the משנה now mixes the places of slaughter.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two חולין, the first outside and the second inside: the first is כשר and פטור; the second brings lashes and is פסול.

steps.title: Both sacred, first outside and second inside
steps.stepSummary: Both animals are קדשים. The first is slaughtered outside the עזרה and the second inside. The first brings כרת, both bring lashes, and both are פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both animals are sacred, and the first is slaughtered outside and the second inside: the first brings כרת, both get the forty lashes, and both are unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה gives another case: two sacred animals, a mother and its child. The first is slaughtered outside the עזרה and the second inside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Slaughtering a sacred animal outside the עזרה brings כרת, so the first animal brings כרת and is ruined as a קרבן. The second, slaughtered inside on the same day as its mother or child, is also פסול, because it cannot be offered on that day. The משנה rules that both bring the forty lashes.

keyTerms.meaning: Sacred animals set aside as קרבנות
A Heavenly punishment of being 'cut off'
Receive the forty lashes (the court punishment of מלקות)
Unfit, here meaning not valid as a קרבן

phrases.english: Sacred animals, outside and inside:
the first is liable to כרת,
and for both of them one receives the forty lashes,
and both of them are unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the משנה's list, now with both animals sacred, first outside then inside.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sacred, first outside and second inside: the first brings כרת, both bring lashes, and both are פסול.

steps.title: Both non-sacred, first inside and second outside
steps.stepSummary: Both animals are חולין. The first is slaughtered inside the עזרה and the second outside. The first is פסול with no punishment; the second brings lashes but is כשר to eat.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both animals are non-sacred, and the first is slaughtered inside and the second outside: the first is unfit and there is no punishment; for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is fit.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה flips the case from step 15. Now two חולין animals: the first is slaughtered inside the עזרה and the second outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A חולין animal slaughtered inside the עזרה is פסול, but there is no punishment for that first slaughter. The second slaughter breaks the rule of אותו ואת בנו, so he gets lashes. Still, the meat of the second is כשר, since slaughtering חולין outside is normal.

phrases.english: Non-sacred animals, inside and outside:
the first is unfit, and he is exempt,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes,
and it is fit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 15: same חולין animals, but the order of inside and outside is reversed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both חולין, first inside and second outside: the first is פסול with no punishment; the second brings lashes but is כשר.

steps.title: Both sacred, first inside and second outside
steps.stepSummary: Both animals are קדשים. The first is slaughtered inside and is a valid קרבן with no punishment. The second, slaughtered outside, brings lashes and is פסול.
steps.simpleTranslation: If both animals are sacred, and the first is slaughtered inside and the second outside: the first is fit and there is no punishment; for the second he gets the forty lashes, and it is unfit.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last case in the משנה: two sacred animals, the first slaughtered inside the עזרה and the second outside.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first was slaughtered the proper way, so it is a good קרבן. The second cannot be offered on the same day as its mother or child, so it is פסול. He gets lashes for אותו ואת בנו. The משנה does not mention כרת for slaughtering it outside, because this animal was not fit to be offered that day anyway.
steps.whatToRemember: The משנה checks every mix of חולין or קדשים, inside or outside, and in each case asks three things: is there כרת, are there lashes, and is the animal fit.

phrases.english: Sacred animals, inside and outside:
the first is fit, and he is exempt,
and for the second he receives the forty lashes,
and it is unfit.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirror image of step 16: the same sacred animals, but the order is reversed (inside first, then outside).
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Both sacred, first inside and second outside: the first is a valid קרבן with no punishment; the second brings lashes and is פסול.

steps.title: Where do we learn that the rule applies to sacred animals?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with a ברייתא that asks for the source that אותו ואת בנו applies to מוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: From where do we know that the rule of 'it and its child' applies to sacred animals?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins. It quotes a ברייתא that asks for the source showing that אותו ואת בנו also applies to sacred animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה said directly that the rule applies 'בחולין ובמוקדשין' (step 6), and its cases gave lashes for sacred animals too. The ברייתא now asks which פסוק teaches the part about sacred animals. This question sets up the answer in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
'It and its child': the ban on slaughtering a mother and its child on the same day

phrases.english: GEMARA: The Rabbis taught:
From where do we know regarding 'it and its child'
that it applies to sacred animals?

steps.triggerLanguage: מִנַּיִן לְאוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ שֶׁנּוֹהֵג בְּמוּקְדָּשִׁין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by asking for the source of the משנה's statement (step 6) that the rule applies to מוקדשין.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The פסוק showing that אותו ואת בנו applies to מוקדשין.

steps.title: The two פסוקים side by side
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא answers: the פסוק about a newborn animal brought as a קרבן comes right before the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו, and this teaches that the rule applies to sacred animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: The verse says: 'A bull or a sheep or a goat, when it is born...', and right after it is written: 'And a bull or a sheep, it and its child you shall not slaughter on one day.' This teaches that 'it and its child' applies to sacred animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers its own question. It points out that the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו comes right after a פסוק about קרבנות.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first פסוק talks about when a newborn animal may be brought as a קרבן. Because the very next פסוק gives the rule of אותו ואת בנו, we learn that this rule also covers sacred animals.

keyTerms.meaning: The פסוק teaches (introduces a proof from a פסוק)

phrases.english: The verse states:

phrases.aramaic: ״שׁוֹר אוֹ כֶשֶׂב אוֹ עֵז כִּי יִוָּלֵד״,
phrases.english: 'A bull or a sheep or a goat, when it is born',
phrases.notes: ויקרא 22:27. That פסוק goes on to say when the animal may be brought as a קרבן.

phrases.english: and it is written after it:
'And a bull or a sheep,

phrases.aramaic: אֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ לֹא תִשְׁחֲטוּ בְּיוֹם אֶחָד״ –
phrases.english: it and its child you shall not slaughter on one day' –
this taught about 'it and its child'
that it applies to sacred animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 19.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The פסוק of אותו ואת בנו comes right after a פסוק about קרבנות, which teaches that the rule applies to מוקדשין.

steps.title: Maybe the rule applies only to sacred animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges: if the rule is learned from the context of קרבנות, maybe it applies only to מוקדשין and not to חולין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: for sacred animals, yes; for non-sacred animals, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the proof. If the context is about קרבנות, maybe the rule is limited to sacred animals only.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The proof worked by placing the rule inside a section about קרבנות. But that same placement could suggest the rule is only about קרבנות. That would leave out חולין, even though we know the rule applies to them.

keyTerms.meaning: But let me say (introduces another way to read it)

phrases.english: But say:
for sacred animals, yes;
for non-sacred animals, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of the פסוקים given in step 20.
steps.kashyaTarget: The proof from the closeness of the two פסוקים.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the context of קרבנות shapes the rule, it might shape it completely and limit it to מוקדשין, leaving out חולין.

steps.title: The word "שור" breaks off the topic
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers that the word "שור" in the second פסוק starts a new topic, so the rule is not limited to קדשים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The word 'bull' broke off the topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The second פסוק says "שור" again, even though the first פסוק already said it, and this shows a new topic is starting.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Repeating "שור" signals that the second פסוק is not simply continuing the topic of קרבנות. So the rule of אותו ואת בנו stands on its own and covers חולין too. It is no longer tied only to קדשים.

keyTerms.meaning: Broke off the topic, starting a new subject
Bull, here the repeated word in the second פסוק

steps.confusionAlert: This answer does not cancel the proof for קדשים. It only shows the rule is not limited to קדשים. The גמרא will next ask how we still know that it includes קדשים.

phrases.english: 'Bull' broke off the topic.
phrases.notes: The first פסוק already mentioned a bull, so saying it again in the next פסוק marks a fresh start.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 21.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading a word in the פסוק as a break in topic
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Since the rule sits in a section about קרבנות, it applies only to מוקדשין.
steps.terutzMaskana: The repeated word "שור" starts a new topic, so the rule also applies to חולין.

steps.title: Maybe the rule applies only to non-sacred animals
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא flips the earlier question: maybe אותו ואת בנו applies to חולין but not to מוקדשין.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say instead: for non-sacred animals, yes; for sacred animals, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The word "שור" broke the topic away from קרבנות, so the rule covers חולין. The גמרא now asks whether that same break means the rule no longer covers מוקדשין at all.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 22, "שור" was read as starting a new topic, so the rule was not limited to קדשים. That answer creates the opposite problem: if the topic is cut off, maybe the rule now applies only to חולין. That would undo the ברייתא's lesson from step 20.

keyTerms.meaning: But say instead (a suggestion of the opposite possibility)

steps.confusionAlert: Don't confuse this with step 21. There the worry was "only קדשים, not חולין." Here it is the reverse: "only חולין, not קדשים."

phrases.english: But say: with non-sacred animals, yes,
with sacred animals, no!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns the answer of step 22 around and raises the opposite problem
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of "שור" as starting a new topic (step 22)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If "שור" fully separates the topic from קרבנות, the rule should apply only to חולין and lose its link to מוקדשין.

steps.title: The letter ו in "ושור" keeps sacred animals included
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says "ושור" with a ו, meaning "and." That ו adds the new topic on top of the first one, so מוקדשין stay included.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is written: "And an ox." The ו adds on to the first topic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the letter ו ("and") connects the פסוק back to the topic of קרבנות. So the rule covers both kinds of animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "שור" opens a new topic, so חולין are included. The ו in front of it adds this to the earlier topic, so מוקדשין stay included too. Both parts of one word together give the full rule.

keyTerms.meaning: The letter ו adds on (it connects to what came before)
The first topic (here, the קרבנות section)

steps.whatToRemember: "שור" brings in חולין, and the ו of "ושור" keeps מוקדשין included. So אותו ואת בנו applies to both.

phrases.english: It is written: "And an ox"
the letter vav adds on to the first topic.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּתִיב: ״וְשׁוֹר״ – וָי״ו מוֹסִיף עַל עִנְיָן רִאשׁוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 23
steps.terutzResolutionType: Precise reading of a letter in the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The break at "שור" might have cut off מוקדשין entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ו links back to the קרבנות topic, so the rule applies to both מוקדשין and חולין.

steps.title: If linked to sacrifices, why does the rule cover mixed breeds?
steps.stepSummary: If the rule is learned from the קרבנות section, maybe it should exclude כלאים, the way קרבנות do. Yet a ברייתא says it applies to כלאים and to a כוי.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, just as כלאים are not valid for קדשים, so too כלאים should not be included in אותו ואת בנו. Why then is it taught in a ברייתא: אותו ואת בנו applies to כלאים and to a כוי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the link to קרבנות. A mixed-breed animal can't be a קרבן, so if the rule is tied to קרבנות, mixed breeds should be left out. But a ברייתא says they are included.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since the ו ties אותו ואת בנו to the קרבנות section, the גמרא suggests the rule should also share the limits of that section. One limit is that כלאים are not fit for the מזבח. The ברייתא contradicts this, because it says the rule applies to כלאים and even to a כוי.

keyTerms.meaning: An animal born from two different species (like a sheep and a goat)
A kosher animal of doubtful status, between a domestic and a wild animal
If just as... so too (drawing a comparison)
Why then? (pointing to a contradicting source)

phrases.english: If so, just as with sacred animals, mixed breeds are not included,

phrases.aramaic: אַף אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ כִּלְאַיִם לָא?
phrases.english: so too with a mother and its offspring, mixed breeds should not be included?
Why then is it taught in a ברייתא:
A mother and its offspring applies
to mixed breeds and to a koy?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי מָה קָדָשִׁים כִּלְאַיִם לָא, אַף אוֹתוֹ וְאֶת בְּנוֹ כִּלְאַיִם לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the link to קרבנות set up in step 24 to raise a new problem
steps.kashyaTarget: The connection of אותו ואת בנו to the קרבנות section
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the rule is tied to קדשים, it should share their exclusion of כלאים. A ברייתא includes כלאים and כוי, which contradicts this.

steps.title: A second problem from the word "sheep"
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא adds another difficulty. The פסוק says "שה," and it is about to bring a teaching of רבא about that word.
steps.simpleTranslation: And furthermore: "sheep" is written, and רבא said:
steps.whatsHappening: This is a setup line. The גמרא is opening a second challenge about כלאים based on the word "שה," and רבא's teaching follows in the next section.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word "ועוד" shows this is an extra attack on the same idea from step 25: why should the rule include כלאים? The proof will come from what רבא learns from the word "שה" in the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו.

keyTerms.meaning: Sheep or goat (the word used in the פסוק)

phrases.english: And furthermore, "sheep" is written,
phrases.notes: This is the word "שה" in the פסוק of אותו ואת בנו (ויקרא 22:28).

phrases.english: and Rava said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second challenge to the one in step 25
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's ruling that אותו ואת בנו applies to כלאים
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The word "שה," as רבא will explain it, seems to exclude כלאים. The full argument continues in the next section.
